claim: This bound version-of-record XML describes consenting healthcare professionals wearing anonymized UWB tags at Le Corbusier Hospital ED, Firminy, France, during 7 March–21 April 2022. Methods says 27 tags and lists eight staff subcategories; Results says 28 tags and reports 16,413,096 timestamped coordinates in 315 sequences. Preserve this 27-versus-28 discrepancy as reported; it is unresolved here. Locations were recorded at 5 Hz as coordinates with timestamps, then aggregated into 10-second windows to reduce noise. The movement measure is hourly walking distance in metres: Euclidean straight-line displacement between coordinates from the same tag, aggregated per hour. This is distance, not elapsed movement time or speed; the described method does not provide speed observations, locomotion-mode-stratified speed evidence, or a route graph/obstacle-constrained path. Staff job subcategories are not patient or locomotion modes. The source does not establish patient mobility or assistance needs, walk/wait/work from location alone, a universal speed, transferability to Cairns, or a per-mode distribution.

primary_source.population: Consenting healthcare professionals (assistant nurses, triage nurses, ICU nurses, waiting-room nurses, short-stay-unit nurses, managers, doctors and on-duty doctors) wearing anonymized tags at Le Corbusier Hospital emergency department, Firminy, France; Methods reports 27 tags while Results reports 28 tags. Patients were not the tracked population.
primary_source.units: Location coordinates and timestamps recorded 5 times per second; smoothing windows of 10 seconds; hourly Euclidean displacement aggregated as distance in metres per hour. No elapsed movement-time measure or speed unit/value is reported by this method.
primary_source.licence_access: Europe PMC fullTextXML snapshot of the open-access article; XML states Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0). Source text is described only; no adapted source material is redistributed.

transformation.description: Read the locally bound Europe PMC XML and extracted source-defined population, sampling cadence, smoothing window and hourly straight-line distance method into a descriptive evidence claim. Kept the Methods/Results tag-count discrepancy explicit. No coordinates were transformed and no numeric speed, mode distribution, fit or default was calculated.
transformation.input_units: Publication XML text; timestamped planar coordinates; 5 Hz sampling; 10-second aggregation windows; metres and hours as stated for the distance measure.
transformation.output_units: Qualitative method/provenance statement distinguishing sampling cadence, smoothing duration, hourly distance, elapsed time and speed; no model speed value.
